KEY MESSAGE 1...Low clouds and rain showers return overnight
into Tuesday night with a rumble of thunder possible. 

Still tracking another band of lower clouds moving south across
our region. Eventually, even these clouds will dry up with the
daytime heating. The same cannot be said for later tonight. A 
backdoor front should arrive from the NE and push well into 
southern New England before a low pressure to our north gets 
close enough to increase southwest winds and drive this front 
back to the north some time Tuesday afternoon into Tuesday 
night.

The main impact will be some lower clouds and perhaps some
patchy drizzle late tonight. A passing shortwave over northern
New England increases the risk for more significant showers the
closer one gets to northern MA. Could even see some rumbles of 
thunder given some weak elevated instability above am inversion,
again with a greater risk towards northern New England.

Persistent east to southeast winds could keep waters level up
towards Nantucket Sound. Will need to monitor the Tuesday
morning high tide. Impacts look marginal right now, so no
headlines at this time. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Isolated shower possible Wednesday, but drier
overall. Dry conditions return for Thursday with seasonably 
cool temperatures.

A trailing cold front shifts across the region Wednesday with
surface high pressure building in from the west through the day. 
Model soundings show increased mixing in the boundary layer
supporting drier conditions and also westerly winds with gusts
20-30 mph. Westerly, downslope flow combined with 925mb
temperatures +17- 18C will support a warm fall day with high
temperatures in the 70s in many areas. There are indications of 
a stray shower or two as a weak wave moves through, but this 
will be fairly limited in coverage and at most a light 
shower/sprinkle due to the drier lower levels.

As high pressure settles in further into Thursday, the airmass
dries out even more. Thursday will likely be dry, although
cooler than Wednesday. A cooler airmass will also have moved in 
with 925mb temperatures around 10C cooler than Wednesday. This 
will yield seasonably cool temperatures mainly in the lower 
60s.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Low pressure system expected to bring rain
Friday into early Saturday. Gusty northwest winds and below 
normal temperatures.

Deterministic and ensemble guidance show a stronger/deeper
northern stream shortwave trough push across the Great Lakes 
and the northeast Friday into Saturday. There is synoptic 
support with this system as an upper level jet positions near 
southern New England yielding large scale ascent while also 
advecting in a plume of above normal moisture northward into the
region. This will set the stage for a widespread rain. Despite 
plentiful moisture, instability appears to be limited thus 
minimizing the potential for heavy rain impacts. Ensemble 
guidance ranges amounts generally from 0.25 to 0.60" with the 
ECMWF and Canadian leaning wetter than the GFS solutions. Across
those particular models, amounts closer to an inch are 
possible. These higher amounts are not out of the question if we
can tap into better forcing with the warm front. Finer details 
such as exact timing of arrival and exit of rain are less 
certain as there are difference across guidance still. Rain more
likely arrives in the Friday morning timeframe, continuing 
overnight. Most guidance shows this system to be fairly 
progressive meaning it won't be lingering the whole weekend. The
bulk of the rain likely exits early Saturday morning. In 
addition, the initial southerly LLJ with this system nudges in 
Friday which if mixed sufficiently, will bring breezy to gusty 
southerly winds (gusts 20-30 mph).

A strong cold front pushes across the region by early Saturday
morning putting the northeast within a classic cold air
advection pattern with gusty NW winds, cooler temperatures, and 
isolated showers. A NW 40-50 kt LLJ positions across the region 
Saturday. The tighter gradient and CAA to help steepen lapse 
rates will support deeper mixing and thus gusty NW winds. The 
degree or mixing and strength of the LLJ are still less certain 
this far out, but ensembles show a signal for gusts 35-45 mph 
possible, potentially higher across the coastal waters. 925mb 
temperatures range between - 2C to +2C Saturday yielding likely 
the coolest temperatures of the season so far. Highs will likely
struggle to get out of the 40s across the interior with low 50s
in the valleys and coastal plain. RH fields show residual
moisture within the cyclonic flow pattern. This may be enough to 
support some isolated showers. Some of the higher elevation 
points across the Berkshires may only hit the 40 degree mark on 
Saturday. It's a bit too early to say the "S word" just yet
(snow). However...if the timing aligns, a morning flurry or
shower can't be ruled out in those higher terrain spots out
west. Expect a cold night Saturday night with high probabilities
